review_notes: Reviewed all 82 lines of the target and inspected the definitions of the complex operator and its real/imaginary projections, plus the RealSmooth conversion and representative uses in RealVolume. The identified simplification opportunity is limited to projection lemmas with demonstrated manual rewrites; I found no supported cycle or unsuitable rewrite direction.

findings.excerpt:
lemma Smooth.ofReal_part_re (f : SmoothRealFunction A) :
    (Smooth.ofReal f).part Complex.reCLM = f :=
  SmoothRealFunction.ext_value rfl

lemma Smooth.ofReal_part_im (f : SmoothRealFunction A) :
    (Smooth.ofReal f).part Complex.imCLM = SmoothRealFunction.constant 0 :=
findings.problem: These conversion/projection equalities have no simp attribute, so simplification does not put the real and imaginary parts of `Smooth.ofReal f` into their natural normal forms. The file immediately has to name both rules explicitly while proving `complexL_ofReal`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to both `Smooth.ofReal_part_re` and `Smooth.ofReal_part_im`, retaining the current left-to-right orientations. This makes `(Smooth.ofReal f).part Complex.reCLM` simplify to `f` and `(Smooth.ofReal f).part Complex.imCLM` simplify to `SmoothRealFunction.constant 0`.
findings.benefit: The normal forms follow the real/imaginary decomposition of an embedded real function, and the existing `complexL_ofReal` proof can use ordinary simplification instead of manually listing these projection rewrites. The right-hand sides do not recreate the left-hand expressions, so these orientations do not introduce a rewrite cycle.
